Hi all —

Thanks for the context. Short technical note below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR- Both AWS PrivateLink (AWS Endpoint Service) and VPC Peering are supported for Redwood Private deployments. For minimal cross-account routing and tighter isolation, we recommend PrivateLink. For very high throughput with simpler routing, VPC Peering may be appropriate.

Details / pros & cons- AWS PrivateLink (recommended)  - Pros: No route table or NAT changes required on customer VPC; exposes a private ENI-backed endpoint in the customer's VPC; easier to satisfy firewall/allowlist requirements because traffic stays on AWS backbone; cross-account access controlled via endpoint/service config.  - Cons: Slightly more operational setup (create endpoint, accept service), and there are per-GB data transfer costs. Supports TLS over 443.

- VPC Peering  - Pros: Native L3 routing, no additional endpoint charges; good for very high throughput where you control routing.  - Cons: Requires route table changes and managing overlapping CIDRs; less isolation (peering is broad inside VPCs unless you use scoped routes); requires coordination if peering across accounts/regions.

IP allowlist / ports- If you choose PrivateLink: typically you only need to allow outbound HTTPS (443) from your app subnets to the VPC endpoint ENIs. We provide the ENI IPs when the endpoint is created; procurement can request "allow outbound TCP 443 to Redwood private endpoint ENIs (to be provided)".
- If you choose VPC Peering: allow the relevant CIDR ranges between the two VPCs and ensure route table entries exist. No public IPs required.

Throughput / sizing notes- Based on the 500-1500 RPS profile (1-2KB payloads): both PrivateLink and peering will comfortably handle this. If you expect sustained 10-20k RPS we should discuss dedicated capacity sizing.

Operational notes- We'll request the following from you to provision the endpoint/peering:   - VPC ID and region for the app VPC  - Preferred subnet(s) for endpoint ENIs (for PrivateLink)  - Contact and process for endpoint acceptance (if cross-account)  - Any firewall ticket format/fields procurement wants included (we can provide a sample text they can paste)

Attachments attached: redwood-private-vpc-design.pdf (diagram + example firewall text), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

Happy to jump on the Fri 7/3 10am PT call to walk the security team through this.
